title: NEW JERSEY RESOURCES NAMED ONE OF AMERICA’S MOST RESPONSIBLE COMPANIES BY NEWSWEEK
body_text: New Jersey Resources NEW JERSEY RESOURCES NAMED ONE OF AMERICA’S MOST RESPONSIBLE COMPANIES BY NEWSWEEK 12/07/2022 - For Immediate Release WALL, NJ – For the fourth consecutive year, New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) was named one of America’s Most Responsible Companies by Newsweek in recognition of its excellence and accomplishments in corporate social responsibility. NJR was selected from a pool of 2,000 companies across 14 industries that were evaluated and ranked based on a detailed analysis of key performance indicators in three areas of corporate social responsibility: environmental, social and corporate governance. The final list recognizes the top most responsible companies in the United States and reinforces NJR’s commitment to corporate sustainability and reputation for service excellence. “New Jersey Resources is committed to advancing a clean energy future by embracing sustainable business practices that meet the energy needs of our customers, benefit the environment and strengthen the communities we serve,” said Steve Westhoven, President and CEO of New Jersey Resources. “It is an honor to be recognized as one of the most responsible companies in the country. This recognition reflects our belief that sustainability and corporate citizenship are good for business, good for our customers and good for the future.” Environmental stewardship and sustainability are priorities for NJR, and the company is committed to achieving net-zero emissions from its New Jersey operations by 2050. Its principal subsidiary, New Jersey Natural Gas, which keeps homes and businesses warm for nearly 570,000 customers throughout New Jersey, is leading the way to help reduce emissions – building the first green hydrogen project on the East Coast; modernizing its infrastructure to build the most environmentally sound delivery systems in the state, as measured by leaks per mile; and helping customers reduce energy consumption through its energy-efficiency initiatives. In addition, NJR’s renewable energy subsidiary Clean Energy Ventures is one of the largest owner/operators of solar projects in the state with over $1 billion invested in building clean, emissions-free power for homes and businesses. To learn more about NJR’s leadership and commitment to sustainability, please visit www.njrsustainability.com . America’s Most Responsible Companies 2023 is a project of Newsweek in partnership with Statista. For more information on the rankings and methodology for selection, please visit newsweek.com/americas-most-responsible-companies-2023 . About New Jersey Resources New Jersey Resources (NYSE: NJR) is a Fortune 1000 company that, through its subsidiaries, provides safe and reliable natural gas and clean energy services, including transportation, distribution, asset management and home services. NJR is composed of five primary businesses: New Jersey Natural Gas , NJR’s principal subsidiary, operates and maintains over 7,700 miles of natural gas transportation and distribution infrastructure to serve over 569,000 customers in New Jersey’s Monmouth, Ocean and parts of Morris, Middlesex and Burlington counties. NJR Clean Energy Ventures invests in, owns and operates solar projects with a total capacity of more than 386 megawatts, providing residential and commercial customers with low-carbon solutions. NJR Energy Services manages a diversified portfolio of natural gas transportation and storage assets and provides physical natural gas services and customized energy solutions to its customers across North America. Storage & Transportation serves customers from local distributors and producers to electric generators and wholesale marketers through its ownership of Leaf River and the Adelphia Gateway Pipeline Project, as well as our 50% equity ownership in the Steckman Ridge natural gas storage facility. NJR Home Services provides service contracts as well as heating, central air conditioning, water heaters, standby generators, solar and other indoor and outdoor comfort products to residential homes throughout New Jersey. NJR and its nearly 1,300 employees are committed to helping customers save energy and money by promoting conservation and encouraging efficiency through Conserve to Preserve® and initiatives such as The SAVEGREEN Project® and The Sunlight Advantage®. For more information about NJR : www. njresources.com . Follow us on Twitter @NJNaturalGas . “Like” us on facebook.com/NewJerseyNaturalGas . title: Agents of Change: PE Associates in the AI Age
summary: For our Agents of Change series, we speak with real decision-makers at investment firms to understand the impact AI is having on finance roles today. Our series kicks off with a profile of the Private Equity Associate, a top destination for some of the most talented investors in private capital. Read on to discover how these leaders are pushing for technological change in the finance industry, and the gaps AI companies need to bridge in order to make a difference.
body_text: We often talk about companies as if they are people, but really, it’s the leaders behind top firms who are the real Agents of Change. That’s what inspired this series, which gets to know the investors and thinkers pushing funds to think of themselves as innovators and early adopters, especially in a market where a slight edge can mean everything. For every wave of technical innovation, there are the innovators who absorb the risk of experimenting with new technologies on behalf of the entire market. It’s often not until a second segment of early adopters help bridge the gap to a broader audience that mass adoption is seen. But by then, many firms, both on the tech side, and the customer side, have already missed an opportunity to be early movers, define the tech in a way that suits them, and get a jump start on capturing its gains. Source: ASAE Center As we spoke with over 100 investors in private equity, we realized it’s often PE associates who are at the forefront, navigating the complexities of investments and being pushed to think about doing things faster, better and smarter. Traditionally, the Associate role is one of the most sought-after destinations for MBAs, junior financial analysts and consultants alike. Their days are filled with financial modeling, due diligence, and direct negotiations – vital tasks that require both deep analytical skills and a nuanced understanding of human relationships – with an almost immediate impact on real businesses. How Is AI Impacting the Associate Role? Today, investor tasks are being augmented by AI, introducing both opportunities and concerns. We have observed that many funds are pulling together innovation teams, with associates often making up the bulk of the group, to think about where to apply new technologies in a way that actually has a practical business impact. In our conversations, we also heard about what we view as less ideal approaches. Some funds are jumping straight into partnership discussions with big names like Microsoft and OpenAI to provide tools like ChatGPT Enterprise or Microsoft Co-Pilot to employees. Others are siloing innovation to a select group of teams and evaluating the impact of new point solutions on a small sample. While these strategies can help, we agree with approaches recommended by AI experts like Ethan Mollick, who started his “flipped learning” model in the classroom, and now recommends similar distributed models to enterprises. In these approaches, employees would be given greater resources and latitude to experiment with AI on their jobs, then come back to their teams to solidify and disperse learned best practices. This also aligns with the “Decentralize” strategy recommendation from the last discussion in our Products & Markets series . In the context of the investing world, where AI use cases are taking shape but often still unrefined, it helps to have the practitioners closest to the subject matter provide input on AI application. Often fresh out of business school or with several years experience at a top investment bank, associates have seen a breadth of scenarios, and have the depth of knowledge to evaluate impact on the ground. To be sure, we decided to interview a handful of associates in greater depth, and kick off our Agents of Change series with perspectives from these powerhouses of PE deal teams. Structure Remains, With Room to Explore Last month, we interviewed four associates across middle market private equity firms, a fund at a major US bank, a small internationally focused firm, and a global mega-fund. While all agreed to share their insights, most also requested to remain anonymous in order to be able to speak freely about their experiences and their firm's respective strategies. Experiences can differ vastly for associates at diverse PE firms, but one common theme we observed is a desire to think and experiment beyond what most funds are doing today. Analysts and associates are still limited in their actual ability to experiment with technology, often due to firm-wide policies, or simply a lack of resources. Many firms we spoke with outright block access to AI tools like ChatGPT. Those who do allow access to LLM-based sites emphasized that they be used primarily for initial research and simple text summarization, never modeling or final outputs. This makes sense given the sensitive nature of the data and the state of most AI-powered point applications today. Because the risk of a deal going south can be outsized, firms maintain rigorous standard operating cadences to reduce the likelihood of an undesirable outcome, whether from. Still, other funds are being smart about structured experimentation. While a narrow approach to testing AI technology may not be as powerful as decentralized adoption, it’s better than nothing at all. Other associates we spoke with mentioned that innovation and testing new approaches is encouraged, but the market is simply not ready to deliver solutions that drive meaningful impact quite yet. Once we dove deeper, it became clear what deal teams need to see before going all-in on AI. Pain Points and Solutions While often described as more manageable than investment banking, workstreams owned by PE associates are still done on a very fast turn-around, especially at smaller funds or those participating as minority investors. “Just about every deal cycle is the same. Our diligence process is very rushed. Typically there is a deadline to submit bids in less than two weeks, and we're just hearing about it on the Friday before”, described one associate we spoke with. To help with this, several ideas surfaced in our conversations: Dashboards : A common theme across all of the requested products we spoke about was enabling greater real-time insights into deal analysis and portfolio operations. “A dashboard, with data refreshed on a weekly or more regular basis, to allow AI to pull in information about sales or operations. Putting it in a format where we can see how the company is performing in real time,” would be a game-changer, per a Senior PE Associate we spoke with. Modeling Assistants: Pilar de la Barra, at the Latam-focused Australis Partners, talked about the potential to increase efficiencies in Excel-based work. “I'm still at a point where I review almost every cell in the model, so figuring out how to efficiently go over some of the technical analysis, that's a rather tedious task that I could see being improved.” Modeling, of course, continues to occupy much of the time of deal teams, with work often spread across VPs, associates and analysts. Though some IT and operations associates talk about the role of AI in analyzing large datasets and rapid scenario modeling, the reality is that little of this is powered by generative AI today. 3rd-Party Data Integrations: While most investors have access to premium market intelligence, and capacity to acquire more on a per-deal basis, the process of bridging the right data into the due diligence and modeling process can still be time consuming, and leaves associates wondering if the data used to supplement their assumptions is the best of what is available. Data coverage creates an opportunity as well, with market data in developed markets being much more readily available than in emerging economies. Still, De la Barra’s involvement in operations and board decisions at Australis' portfolio companies underscores a trend in which firms are increasingly curious about technological tools to streamline operations and enhance decision-making. As emerging markets in Latin America continue to grow, with Colombia's PE market expanding by over 15% in the last year alone, the integration of sophisticated tools could become essential in remaining competitive with North American firms. Barriers to Adoption While some investment associates facing these pain points are eagerly pushing for solutions, many are also more realistic and measured in their optimism for AI. Perhaps due to the incentive structure in private equity, even entry level investors feel a strong degree of ownership over their work, and are highly tuned into the concerns of central management related to feasibility, compliance and operations. Privacy and data integrity are major examples of such concerns, where even associates who would not be directly affected by data leakage or IP issues are aware that deal information must be handled very securely. More relevant to the analysis itself, investors are typically among the two-thirds of knowledge workers aware of issues with hallucination and inaccurate data in LLM training data. “We are very wary of where we are getting our data from”, mentioned an associate at a major bank. Associates at internationally focused funds described working on the front lines of deciphering data in different formats and diverse operating norms across different markets. Nonetheless, they are often not quite ready to trust AI solutions in without significant human oversight. The result? One associate tells us, “honestly, we're still pretty old school. We use AI in basic tasks like writing internal memos or summarizing news, but today, not much more.” Taking the First Step The operational involvement of PE associates varies significantly between firms, influenced heavily by the size and focus of the fund. Some roles are more narrowly defined, focusing on financial analysis without direct operational control, which is typical in larger funds where investments are more about financial structuring rather than operational turnaround. Here, AI can serve as a critical tool in managing complex global portfolios, offering real-time insights that were previously unattainable. In theory, these larger firms could see faster gains from automation as work is already more clearly defined and operationalized. For instance, AI tools are being leveraged to perform rapid due diligence, a task that some noted involves "stress tests" on financial models provided by potential investment targets. Such tools not only speed up the process but also enhance the accuracy of projections and risk assessments. Associates we spoke with at smaller firms often talked about wearing many hats, and, in some cases even participating in conversations at the firm leadership level, which might be too complex to benefit from AI just yet, or at least require more custom-tailored applications. For now, it is unclear whether AI will serve to further entrench economies of scale at large funds, or help make smaller funds more competitive. Perhaps the answer is both. Nonetheless, a top debate in AI continues to be whether the technology will ultimately add value and create new roles by enabling novel capabilities, or simply make processes more efficient and possibly slow hiring for knowledge work roles. As you might expect, associates talented enough to make it into leading PE funds do not see their work as being immediately replaceable by AI, nor should they. When investors look at the technology, those we spoke with see opportunities to automate away some of the busy work or become more competitive in their roles, rather than see entire steps of the process disappear. As one associate from a large cap fund told us, “ at the end of the day, PE associates are energized by their roles and want to do them better, not less often."

title: 7 Sales Tactics To Help Your Business in 2026
summary: Discover 7 powerful sales tactics to grow your business in 2026. Boost revenue, improve outreach, and close more deals with proven strategies.
body_text: Sales tactics have evolved since 81% of buyers now research products before they contact sales representatives. The strategies that worked yesterday might not deliver results tomorrow in today's competitive marketplace. Research shows that 92% of consumers trust referrals from people they know. Sales methods need to adapt therefore. Strong customer relationships and increased word-of-mouth referrals emerge from effective sales techniques. McKinsey's research reveals that strategic sales tactics such as upselling and cross-selling boost sales by up to 20% and revenue by up to 30%. We have gathered 7 powerful sales tactics that will drive your business success in 2026. These strategies are not just theories they are proven approaches that work in today's buying environment. These tactics will give you the competitive edge you need to refine your existing sales strategies or reshape your approach completely. What are top 7 sales tactics in 2026? Companies that treat sales as continuous learning will thrive in 2026. They create cultures where coaching matters more than pressure. These organizations design for agility rather than perfection and see AI as a partner in human connection. Tactic 1: Start with active listening to understand buyer needs Active listening is the life-blood of effective selling in 2026. Studies show that top sales performers talk less and listen more, with a talk-to-listen ratio of 43:57. This helps them sell 120% above quota. This radical alteration from pitching to understanding buyer needs forms the foundation for all other sales tactics . Why listening matters more than pitching Active listening means you listen to understand rather than waiting for your turn to speak. This key difference turns ordinary conversations into meaningful exchanges that build trust and credibility. Research shows that 69% of buyers expect sales representatives to listen to their needs first. Yet this is the trait buyers say they see least often in salespeople. Prioritizing listening does more than make prospects feel good. Active listening: Builds rapport - People appreciate being heard, especially during important business decisions Establishes control - You can adjust tactics live by focusing on the conversation instead of your pitch Creates trust - B2B purchases affect buyers' careers, and they trust only those who understand their challenges Here's something to think about: You show that relationships matter more than sales when you focus on understanding instead of rushing to present solutions. This buyer-first approach sets top performers apart from average ones. How to ask the right questions Good listening starts with questions that encourage prospects to share meaningful information . You can uncover business value that motivates action with three types of strategic questions : Open-ended questions - These are a great way to get prospects talking about their situation Probing questions - Guide buyers to find their top priorities themselves Confirming questions - Verify the shared information to ensure mutual understanding The best approach needs 5-10 thoughtful questions. These help identify problems on the prospect's radar, how these issues affect their business, and unique solutions your company offers. On top of that, follow-up questions show your interest and desire to understand completely. Unlike traditional sales approaches, you shouldn't push toward your pitch but let prospects lead. A sales coach puts it well: you want prospects to ask, "Is that something you can help me with?" Reading between the lines: verbal and nonverbal cues Prospects communicate through non-verbal signals even when they don't state their thoughts directly. Research shows that eye contact between 60-70% of the time builds optimal rapport . People who like or agree with you naturally increase their eye contact duration. Watch for these telling signals: Facial expressions - Agreement shows in smiling and nodding; disagreement appears as compressed lips, lowered eyebrows, or a tense mouth Body positioning - Open arms indicate receptivity, while turned shoulders signal disengagement Mirroring behavior - Prospects who mirror your posture or gestures likely agree with you Video calls play a vital role in remote selling because they let you observe these important visual cues. You miss valuable information that could help address concerns before they become objections without seeing the prospect. The most valuable insights come from both what people say and how they express it. You'll position yourself as a trusted advisor rather than just another salesperson by mastering both verbal and nonverbal signals . Tactic 2: Use storytelling to build emotional connection Storytelling is one of your most powerful sales tools. Research shows 80% of consumers value brands that tell stories. Your ability to craft compelling narratives will be vital for sales success in 2026. A good story can turn basic features and data into an emotional experience that stays with prospects long after your meeting . What makes a good sales story The best sales stories follow clear patterns that guide prospects through their experience. Sales professionals use frameworks like EPIC (Engage, Problem, Impact, Change) or SCIPAB (Situation, Complication, Implication, Position , Action, Benefit) to show how their solutions solve specific challenges. Your customer should be the hero of every story not your product or company. Your brand plays a vital supporting role by providing tools and helping save the day when needed. This shows prospects that their needs come first. Details make your stories come alive. A sales expert puts it well: " Vague : 'One of my clients came to us frustrated because their online sales had plateaued.' Specific: 'A small wedding catering business owner called me after losing a big wedding to a competitor. Frantic, she explained that online sales had dropped 53% over the last month, despite spending $5,000 on a new landing page.'" Emotions drive buying decisions. Research confirms that emotional responses to messages affect purchase decisions more than the actual content. Your stories should tap into feelings that match your prospect's situation. Examples of sales strategies using storytelling Customer success stories work best when tailored to your audience. To cite an instance, an IT company selling cybersecurity software might tell a story about "Smith & Associates ," a mid-size law firm that thought they were too small for cybercriminals until a devastating breach cost them millions. This story taps into real fears without using scare tactics. Personal stories create genuine connections that set you apart from others. Sales teams who share relevant experiences build trust and show empathy. These stories should be brief, genuine, and relate to the prospect's needs. Company origin stories show your brand's human side and values. All the same, use them less often as they don't appeal as much as other stories. Keep them under a minute and share only when asked or when they support key points. When to use stories in the sales process Stories work well throughout the sales trip. During discovery calls, client anecdotes show you understand their challenges and can help solve them. Later on, stories help build trust and address concerns . To cite an instance, when prospects worry about integration, you might say: "We actually had a Head of Marketing with the same fear. Like you, they were using five different tools for email marketing. What they found was that our solution was easy to integrate and allowed them to cancel three of their subscriptions." Build a mental collection of customer stories sorted by pain points, objections, and results. This helps you share relevant examples naturally during talks. Combined with active listening , you'll become a trusted advisor instead of just another sales rep. Once you become skilled at sales storytelling, you'll build emotional connections that data alone can't create—turning interested prospects into loyal customers. Tactic 3: Leverage social proof with testimonials and case studies Social proof has become the life-blood of successful selling . Studies show that 88% of consumers trust user reviews as much as personal recommendations. This psychological principle makes use of our natural tendency to follow others' decisions especially when today's buyers are skeptical. Why social proof works Trust and credibility are the foundations of any successful sale. Your potential buyers feel more confident about their purchase decisions when they see others having great experiences with your product. This confidence comes from basic human nature we naturally look at what others do to figure out what's right. The numbers tell a compelling story about how well social proof works: 59% of consumers look at 2-3 review sites before they buy Testimonials can boost sales page conversions by up to 34% Websites with testimonials get 45% more traffic than those without 70% of people trust recommendations from strangers This trust factor matters even more in B2B sales, where 29% of buyers say case studies are their most important research resource. Companies that use social proof well can cut their customer acquisition costs by 20-50% compared to other channels. How to choose the right customer story? You need to think over carefully when picking customer stories . A good starting point is to identify the challenges you want to highlight. One expert puts it this way: "Look for stories where customers achieved exceptional results, overcame tough challenges, or used your product in unique ways". Here are key selection criteria: Relevance : Pick stories that match your target audience's industry, size, and challenges Performance : Showcase customers who got measurable results Credibility : Use well-known brands when you can, but authentic stories matter more than big names Diversity : Show different scenarios across various industries and applications Look for "brand advocates" who get amazing results with your product. These happy customers usually provide the most powerful testimonials and case studies. Sales tactics examples using metrics and ROI Adding specific metrics to your social proof creates compelling sales tools. To cite an instance, see Cisco's case study about VTNZ, which clearly showed 20% cost savings through Cisco's services. This gives prospects a clear picture of what they could achieve. Ring Logix showed how they helped Propel Technologies handle 95% of support tickets within minutes while offering prices 30% lower than competitors. These concrete numbers make abstract benefits real and convincing. B2B buyers need detailed technical proof with measurable outcomes . Your case studies should follow this proven structure: Problem/Challenge : Define the customer's problem clearly Solution : Show how your product solved their challenge Results : Share specific numbers and measurable outcomes Customer Quote : Add a genuine statement from the customer Video testimonials have ended up being the most effective sales tactics, with 79% of people watching them to learn about companies. Two-thirds of people say they're more likely to buy after seeing a video testimonial that shows how a solution helped someone like them. When you add testimonials and case studies to your sales approach strategically, you create what one sales expert calls "proof that can't be replicated by competitors". This makes social proof more than just a good sales tactic it becomes one of your strongest competitive advantages. Tactic 4: Personalize your outreach using CRM data Customers expect personal attention from brands. Research shows 76% want to build close relationships through personalized interactions. Your bottom line benefits directly - 80% of people buy more after getting a personalized experience. Using CRM to tailor your message A Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system helps you personalize effectively. Sales teams can access a complete dashboard with vital data about prospects and customers. Your team can move past generic approaches by using: Industry-specific challenges - Address pain points unique to each sector Company size and goals - Match outreach to how organizations work and what they want Previous interactions - Build on past conversations and website visits Technology stack - Connect with their current tools and show integration benefits The right CRM marketing platform transforms raw customer data into hundreds of live segments that update immediately. Your team can then communicate precisely across all customer touchpoints. Avoiding generic pitches Name-dropping in email subject lines isn't enough for true personalization. A sales expert puts it well: "It's a continuous outreach plan tailored to each prospect's wants, needs, and preferences". Each prospect deserves at least one unique sentence in every message. Recent LinkedIn posts , company news, or industry updates show you've done your homework and care about their business. People respond better to messages crafted just for them. Take time to review their LinkedIn profiles, social media activity, and public information. The extra effort pays off - personalized messages can boost responses by up to 50% . Salesman tactics that feel personal Smart sales teams balance automation with authenticity . Time your interactions well and make them relevant. Messages should connect to specific actions or information from prospects. Did someone download your whitepaper? Send them a quick summary of key points or discuss the concepts they read. This builds rapport through meaningful exchanges instead of pushy sales tactics. Your customers need to feel valued and heard. Data shows 71% of consumers hate impersonal interactions. Look at your CRM data to spot specific needs and challenges. Then position your solution as the natural fix to their problems. Tactic 5: Use automation and AI to save time and boost accuracy AI and automation will provide decisive competitive advantages by 2026. Sales representatives spend just 25% of their time selling according to research. Teams can double their selling time and achieve 30% higher win rates by using AI tools. Best sales tactics using AI tools Smart teams are using several AI-powered tactics to boost their sales: Evidence-based extraction : AI tracks customer interactions through email, calendars, and collaboration tools without human input. This helps 44% of AI-using salespeople create tailored outreach messages efficiently. Sales call improvement : AI tools study conversations and provide instant insights, highlight crucial moments, and detect patterns in buyer behavior. Nearly 45% of sales professionals use conversation intelligence to coach their teams. Better workflows : AI will initiate 95% of seller research workflows by 2027, compared to less than 20% in 2024. Sales reps can now concentrate on activities that matter most instead of manual research. Smart lead scoring : AI spots patterns in successful conversions to qualify leads automatically, boosting conversion rates by 30%. This helps 47% of sales professionals who use AI qualify leads better . Examples of automation in prospecting Smart automation turns time-consuming prospecting into strategic outreach: Intelligent follow-ups : Smart systems send follow-up messages based on prospect actions . Research shows that responses within five minutes make conversions eight times more likely. Meeting coordination : AI removes email back-and-forth by finding the best meeting times and syncing with calendars. Website monitoring : AI watches visitor behavior and alerts sales reps instantly when quality leads appear. Multi-channel outreach : Modern tools create unified campaigns that blend email and social media outreach. You can explore Persana.ai to find AI-driven engagement tools for advanced personalization. Avoiding over-automation: keeping the human touch AI brings great benefits, but the human element remains vital: Smart timing : Successful sales teams use AI to spot behavior signals that need human interaction. Clear boundaries : Good implementation separates AI tasks (data entry, reminders, alerts) from human responsibilities (strategy, relationships). Honest communication : Customers appreciate transparency about AI usage. Campaigns that acknowledge both AI's strengths and limits often appeal more to audiences. Genuine connection : Outreach should feel authentic despite automation 71% of customers dislike impersonal interactions. Successful organizations see AI as a tool that makes human connections stronger by handling routine work. This allows salespeople to focus on what truly matters building relationships . Tactic 6: Follow up consistently and keep your promises Becoming skilled at follow-up is what sets top performers apart from average salespeople. Studies show that 80% of sales require at least five follow-ups to close the deal. Almost half of sales professionals (48%) never follow up after their original contact. Why follow-up is a good sales tactic? The numbers paint a clear picture. Only 2% of sales close during the first interaction. This means you could miss 98% of your business without proper follow-up. Follow-up keeps you visible when prospects are ready to buy and shows your genuine interest in earning their business. Follow-up goes beyond persistence . Each touchpoint is a chance to deliver value, address concerns, and guide prospects through their buying experience. Of course, this consistent contact helps establish you as a thoughtful partner rather than just another vendor pushing for a sale. How to follow through without being pushy? The perfect balance between persistence and pestering comes from these principles: Be polite, persistent, and patient in every interaction Confirm next steps at the end of each conversation to avoid ambiguity Vary communication channels based on prospect priorities Provide something valuable with each follow-up (relevant case study, industry insight) Schedule calls at agreed-upon times (42% of people are more likely to buy this way) Timing plays a crucial role. A gap of 2-3 days between original follow-ups works well. Then gradually extend the time between touches if you don't receive responses. This measured approach shows professionalism while respecting the prospect's time. Avoiding aggressive sales tactics Aggressive tactics damage your reputation and effectiveness . Repeatedly calling uninterested prospects or using hard-sell approaches don't work. In fact, 57% of people say they're more likely to purchase when salespeople don't apply pressure during follow-ups. Customer trust is built on kept promises. Your ability to deliver on commitments both explicit and implied creates a sense of belonging and loyalty. Breaking promises spreads through negative word-of-mouth and can cause more damage than a direct negative experience. Note that follow-up should add value, not seem desperate. Adding genuine value with each interaction positions you as a trusted advisor worthy of your prospect's business. Tactic 7: Ask for referrals at the right time The success of referral programs depends heavily on timing. Studies show that poor timing can derail even the best referral programs and hurt conversion rates. Trust and momentum are the two key ingredients that make referrals work. When to ask for a referral These moments work best to request referrals: After successful delivery - The product arrival creates peak satisfaction Following positive feedback - Customers give high ratings or NPS scores between 9-10 Post-milestone achievement - You help clients crack tough problems After repeat purchases - Your brand has earned their trust Within 30-45 days of purchase - You can tap into their early excitement The post-renewal period gives you another great chance. A customer's decision to renew shows they're happy enough to recommend others. How to make it easy for customers to refer? Your referral success rates will jump when you make the process simple. Here's what works: Give them ready-to-use messages they can forward to their network. This saves their time and keeps your message clear. Simple referral links or forms make sharing quick and easy. A gentle follow-up after good experiences gets results . To name just one example, see what happens when you say: "I'm glad we could solve this for you. Do you know anyone else who might benefit from similar support?" Incentives that work The right rewards turn happy customers into brand champions . These incentives get results: Rewards that benefit both sides - the referrer and their friend. Store credits push repeat purchases and boost customer value. PayPal cash rewards give instant gratification. Research shows customers expect at least $21 or an 11% discount as a referral reward. The best rewards match your customer base's preferences - some value exclusive perks more than money. Conclusion Success in sales by 2026 will require a perfect blend of human touch and advanced technology. This piece explores seven powerful tactics that will revolutionize your sales results . Active listening builds meaningful relationships, while storytelling creates emotional bonds that numbers alone can't match. Case studies and testimonials provide social proof that makes buying decisions easier for prospects . Your prospects feel valued when you craft personalized messages using CRM data , not just another target. AI and automation tools help your team skip administrative tasks and spend more time building relationships. Regular follow-ups show your reliability and dedication to solving customer problems. Smart timing of referral requests multiplies your sales opportunities through trusted connections. Top-performing sales teams see these tactics as connected parts of a complete strategy. Companies looking to implement advanced personalization can check out Persana to streamline their process with AI-driven engagement features. Note that sales excellence adapts continuously. The digital world will evolve past 2026, but core principles stay the same - understanding customers, building trust, and delivering real value . Teams that adopt new technology while maintaining authentic connections will outshine those stuck with old methods. Sales success boils down to one truth: people buy from those they trust. These seven tactics help you earn that trust naturally and systematically, whatever changes occur in buying behaviors over time. FAQ People often ask me about the best ways to sell in today's market. Here are some common questions I get based on my experience. What are tactics in sales? Sales tactics are specific techniques that help move prospects through the buying process . These methods range from prospecting strategies to closing techniques that handle objections. Good tactics should line up with what customers need instead of pushing products they don't want. While strategies focus on long-term plans, tactics are the immediate actions that fit into these bigger plans. What is a great but underrated sales tactic that works for you? Question-based selling doesn't get enough credit despite its power . You build genuine trust by asking thoughtful, open-ended questions before jumping into your pitch. This helps you discover real needs. The right questions turn simple transactions into valuable consultations. What is the most creative sales tactic you have seen implemented? A software company's clever approach stands out. They sent prospects incomplete puzzles with a note saying "We have the missing piece to complete your business." This tangible metaphor sparked curiosity without being pushy. Another smart tactic involved sending tailored video messages that addressed specific challenges found through research. Consolidated financial performance Net income of $14.3 million increased $2.2 million compared to 1Q 2026, and earnings per share - diluted of $0.87 increased $0.14 per share from 1Q 2026. Net income increased $1.1 million, or 8.5%, compared to $13.1 million, or $0.78 per diluted share, for 2Q 2025. 2Q 2026 Core net income(1) of $14.3 million, or $0.87 per diluted share, increased $2.2 million, or 18.6%, from 1Q 2026 Core net income of $12.0 million, or $0.73 per diluted share. 2Q 2026 Core net income increased $0.1 million from 2Q 2025 Core net income of $14.2 million. 2Q 2026 Core net income excluding purchase accounting accretion ("PAA") was $14.0 million, an increase of $0.8 million from 2Q 2025 Core net income excluding PAA of $13.2 million. Quarterly net interest income: Net interest income of $50.9 million increased $1.5 million, or 3.1% (not annualized), compared to 1Q 2026, and increased $3.3 million, or 6.9%, year-over-year. Interest income of $70.0 million increased $2.0 million, or 2.9% (not annualized), compared to 1Q 2026, and increased $5.4 million, or 8.3%, year-over-year. The increase from 1Q 2026 was primarily driven by a $0.9 million increase from OpenSky™ due to higher balances and higher yields, $1.0 million from the Commercial Bank driven by $0.5 million from interest bearing cash income, $0.4 million from investment securities, and $0.2 million from loan growth. The increase year-over-year was primarily driven by $3.8 million from the Commercial Bank due to strong organic loan growth, and $1.5 million from OpenSky™ due to strong growth from the unsecured loan product. Interest income included $0.2 million from net PAA in 2Q 2026, compared to $0.3 million in 1Q 2026 and $0.4 million in net PAA in 2Q 2025. The increase of $0.5 million compared to 1Q 2026, was primarily driven by growth in the deposit portfolio, and a shift in deposit mix to money markets accounts. The increase of $2.1 million year-over-year was driven by $1.0 million from higher balances and a shift in deposit mix, $0.8 million of lower PAA, and $0.3 million of higher borrowing costs. Interest expense included a $0.1 million benefit from net PAA in 2Q 2026, compared to a $0.1 million benefit in 1Q 2026. There was a $0.9 million benefit from net PAA in 2Q 2025. Quarterly provision: The 2Q 2026 provision for credit losses was $3.6 million, an increase of $0.6 million from 1Q 2026. Net charge-offs totaled $3.8 million, or 0.50% of portfolio loans (annualized), up from $3.0 million or 0.40% of portfolio loans (annualized), in 1Q 2026. Net charge-offs in the quarter include $2.9 million from OpenSky™ loans and $0.9 million from Commercial Bank loans. Net charge-offs for the Commercial Bank increased $1.0 million quarter-over-quarter primarily due to a $0.7 million recovery in 1Q 2026. OpenSky™ net charge-offs amounted to $2.9 million in 2Q 2026 compared to $3.1 million in 1Q 2026. At June 30, 2026, the ACL Coverage Ratio was 1.76%, down 5 bps from March 31, 2026. Quarterly fee revenue: Fee Revenue of $14.4 million increased $1.0 million, compared to 1Q 2026 and increased $1.3 million year-over-year. The increase of $1.0 million during 2Q 2026 was the result primarily of a $1.0 million increase in government loan servicing and packaging revenue (Windsor™), a $0.4 million increase in mortgage banking revenue, and a $0.3 million increase in government lending revenue, offset by a $0.3 million decrease in credit card fees and a $0.2 million decrease in loan servicing rights. The year-over-year fee revenue increase of $1.3 million was primarily due to an increase in government loan servicing and packaging revenue (Windsor™). Fee revenue mix(1) was 22.0% of total revenue for 2Q 2026, compared to 21.3% during 1Q 2026, and 21.6% during 2Q 2025. Quarterly noninterest expense: Noninterest expense of $43.2 million decreased $0.5 million compared to 1Q 2026 and increased $3.6 million compared to 2Q 2025. Core noninterest expense(2) of $43.2 million decreased $0.5 million compared to 1Q 2026 and increased $5.0 million compared to 2Q 2025. Core comparisons include: The decrease of $0.5 million quarter-over-quarter was primarily driven by the following: $0.8 million lower professional fees, attributable to a decrease in consulting expenses and lower audit and accounting related fees; partially offset by a $0.4 million increase in occupancy and costs associated with software upgrades. Year-over-year expense growth of $5.0 million was driven by increases in professional fees associated with investments in shared services areas and OpenSky™, expense associated with headcount growth, increased occupancy and equipment costs and an increase in loan processing costs. Quarterly income taxes: Income tax expense of $4.2 million, or 22.8% of pre-tax income for 2Q 2026, increased $0.4 million from $3.9 million, or 24.3% of pre-tax income for 1Q 2026. The effective income tax rate change quarter-over-quarter primarily reflects refinement of the quarterly tax provision following an updated estimate related to the deferred tax liability associated with fixed assets acquired in the IFH acquisition. Total assets: Total assets of $3.9 billion at June 30, 2026 increased $81.5 million, or 8.6% (annualized) from March 31, 2026. Total assets growth year-over-year was $501.3 million, or 14.8%. The growth quarter-over-quarter, and year-over-year, was primarily driven by increases in portfolio loans, and cash balances. Gross loan growth through July 15th(1) of $159.2 million brings year-to-date loan growth to 10.0% (annualized). C&l loans, plus owner-occupied CRE loans, totaled 37.4% of total portfolio loans at June 30, 2026, 38.3% at March 31, 2026, and 37.6% at June 30, 2025. The accumulated other comprehensive income (loss) on the investment securities portfolio declined $0.1 million during the quarter to $6.3 million after-tax as of June 30, 2026, which represents 1.5% of total stockholders' equity. The Company does not have a held-to-maturity investment securities portfolio. Liquidity: The Company maintains stable and diversified sources of contingent liquidity, generally consistent with prior quarter. Total available borrowing capacity as of June 30, 2026 was $801.6 million, compared to $809.5 million as of March 31, 2026, consisting of $699.4 million of available collateralized borrowing capacity, $96.0 million of unsecured lines of credit with other banks, and $6.2 million of unpledged investment securities available to collateralize potential additional borrowings. Including cash and cash equivalents of $418.3 million, total liquidity was approximately $1.2 billion. Capital: As of June 30, 2026, the Company reported a Common Equity Tier-1 capital ratio of 13.14% and a Tier 1 leverage ratio of 10.59%, compared to 12.92% and 10.48%, respectively, at March 31, 2026. At June 30, 2026, the Company and the Bank maintained regulatory capital ratios that exceed all capital adequacy requirements. Shares repurchased and retired during the three months ended June 30, 2026, as part of the Company's stock repurchase program, totaled 1,213 shares at an average price of $30.03, for a total cost of $36 thousand. As of June 30, 2026, there was $12.4 million remaining to be repurchased under the current $15.0 million authorization repurchase program, which will expire on December 31, 2026 . Financial Metrics Net Interest Margin: NIM of 5.64% for 2Q 2026, decreased 7 bps compared to the prior quarter, and decreased 40 bps year-over-year. Core NIM(1) of 4.04% decreased 11 bps (but decreased 9 bps when excluding PAA) compared to the prior quarter, and decreased 38 bps year-over-year. Net PAA for 2Q 2026 was 3 bps for NIM and 4 bps for Core NIM(1). The decrease quarter-over-quarter in Core NIM includes 3 bps from lower deferred origination fees and net PAA and 3 bps from one non-performing loan relationship. The average yield on interest earning assets of 7.75% decreased 11 bps compared to the prior quarter and decreased 44 bps year-over-year. The decrease quarter-over-quarter was primarily due to the Commercial Bank loan portfolio. The decrease year-over-year was primarily due to the impact of changes in the rate environment to the Commercial Bank and OpenSky™ portfolios, as well as lower loan PAA for the Commercial Bank. The Core Loan Yield(1) of 6.77% for 2Q 2026 decreased 16 bps compared to 1Q 2026, and decreased 37 bps year-over-year. The decrease quarter-over-quarter includes 5 bps from lower deferred origination fees and loan PAA, and 4 bps from one non-performing loan relationship. The decrease year-over-year was primarily a result of changes in the rate environment offsetting organic portfolio growth. The total cost of deposits of 2.29% for 2Q 2026 decreased 5 bps compared to the prior quarter and decreased 7 bps year-over-year. The decrease quarter-over-quarter was primarily due to a shift in product mix, and the decrease year-over-year was primarily due to a shift in product mix as well as changes in the rate environment. The total cost of interest-bearing deposits of 3.09% for 2Q 2026 decreased 8 bps quarter-over-quarter, and decreased 20 bps year-over-year. The decrease quarter-over-quarter was primarily due to a shift in product mix, and the decrease year-over-year was primarily due to a shift in product mix as well as changes in the rate environment. The acquired IFH portfolio decrease reflected $4.7 million of nonaccrual loan resolutions, partially offset by $1.0 million of new nonaccruals. Nonperforming assets increased $24.7 million or 49 bps year-over-year, mainly due to the $15.9 million increase during 3Q 2025 from two loan relationships acquired as part of the IFH transaction and the $9.7 million increase during 2Q 2026 related to the legacy bank loan relationship referenced above. Through July 15, 2026, management did not identify any significant changes in nonperforming assets, special mention loans, or substandard loans from June 30, 2026. title: Story named director of industrial accounts at Entergy Arkansas
summary: Entergy Arkansas has promoted Bentley Story to director of industrial accounts.
body_text: LITTLE ROCK, Ark. – Entergy Arkansas has promoted Bentley Story to director of industrial accounts, where he will lead the company’s efforts to further support some of the utility’s largest customers and state’s largest employers, while supporting continued growth. In this role, Story will focus on enhancing service for key industrial accounts and expanding the company’s managed accounts portfolio. He draws on extensive experience working with major customers, including from his time as a senior project manager and a decade as director of business development at the Arkansas Economic Development Commission. Story holds a bachelor’s degree in business and an MBA from the University of Arkansas. His background also includes roles with the Department of Finance and Administration and Tyson Foods. He is a certified economic developer and a graduate of the Economic Development Institute. About Entergy Arkansas Entergy generates, transmits and distributes electricity to power life for more than 3 million customers through our operating companies in Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi and Texas. We’re focused on keeping costs for our customers as low as possible while providing reliable energy that our communities count on. We’re also investing in growth for the future with a more resilient, cleaner energy system that includes modern natural gas, nuclear and renewable energy generation. As a nationally recognized leader in sustainability and corporate citizenship, we deliver more than $100 million in economic benefits each year to the communities we serve through philanthropy, volunteerism and advocacy. Entergy is a Fortune 500 company headquartered in New Orleans, Louisiana, and has approximately 12,000 employees. Learn more at Entergy.com and connect with @Entergy on social media. title: Digital transformation in insurance report 2030 shaping nextgen models - Wipro
summary: Digital transformation in insurance driving nextgen insurance, ecosystem integration, automation, and data intelligence, enabling customer centric growth
body_text: Industry Futures: Insurance by 2030 Wipro’s Industry Futures report highlights the future of insurance as a shift toward nextgen insurance models driven by hyper-personalization, data intelligence, and ecosystem integration by 2030. Emerging technologies like AI, blockchain, IoT, and parametric insurance will transform insurance operations, risk assessment, underwriting, and claims automation, enabling digital transformation in insurance while fostering climate resilience and sustainability for customer-centric innovation and agile growth. Download Report NextGen Insurance Nextgen insurance will shift from static policies to real-time, AI-driven coverage. Hyper-personalized insurance will leverage generative AI and predictive analytics to dynamically tailor policies based on individual user behavior, offering a bespoke experience. Nextgen insurance will also include usage-based insurance, utilizing IoT and telematics for pay-as-you-use models, transforming auto and health coverage. In the future of insurance, immersive insurance within the metaverse will enable virtual risk assessments and advisory services. Moreover, Insurance-as-a-Service will offer flexible, subscription-based coverage, allowing users to activate or pause policies instantly through AI-powered apps, moving away from rigid long-term contracts. Insurance Ecosystem In the future, the insurance ecosystem will be seamlessly integrated into digital landscapes. Insurance marketplace platforms will leverage cloud, AI and IoT in insurance to connect insurers, brokers, and consumers, offering real-time policy comparisons and instant underwriting. Embedded insurance will naturally weave protection into e-commerce, mobility, and fintech apps, such as ride-sharing platforms that auto-enroll drivers in microinsurance. Alternative distribution partnerships with OEMs, insurtech, and tech giants will enable device-based insurance (e.g., smart home warranties). Meanwhile, open insurance, driven by API frameworks, will allow secure data sharing, fostering innovation and personalized offerings. The digital transformation in insurance will redefine the insurance ecosystem, making it more interconnected and customer-centric. Autonomous Operations Future insurance operations will be autonomous, intelligent, and trustless, driven by AI and blockchain. Agentic advisors will act as virtual agents, offering real-time policy recommendations and claims assistance. Automated underwriting and pricing, leveraging AI, machine learning, and real-time data, will dynamically assess risk, reducing approval times from days to seconds. Intelligent claims processing, enabled by computer vision and IoT, will automate damage assessment, such as AI-driven car crash evaluations. Decentralized contracts will enable self-executing policies, ensuring instant payouts with zero manual intervention, transforming insurance operations. Insurance Data Intelligence As the insurance landscape evolves, data will drive intelligent operations, enabling real-time risk assessments and seamless claims processing. Connected insurance will monitor risks through IT and wearables, allowing insurers to offer proactive coverage tailored to individual needs. Decentralized data systems will secure data sharing, reducing fraud. Real-time assessments, leveraging AI, drones, and geospatial analytics, will automate damage inspections, expediting claim approvals. Meanwhile, insurance telematics 2.0, driven by 5G and smartphone-based sensors data, will create holistic risk profiles that extend beyond driving behavior, encompassing health, mobility, and property insurance. Insurance analytics solutions will play a pivotal role in enhancing decision-making and operational efficiency. Sustainability & Climate Resiliency Insurers will play a key role in driving sustainability and climate adaptation. Sustainable insurance solutions will leverage AI and ESG analytics to incentivize eco-friendly behaviors, such as offering lower premiums for electric vehicle owners. Sustainable assets and investments, guided by green finance frameworks, will redirect capital towards climate-positive projects. Parametric insurance will utilize IoT and satellite data to enable instant payouts during climate disasters. Meanwhile, climate tech risk management will integrate predictive modeling and geospatial AI to help businesses proactively mitigate risks from extreme weather events, fostering a resilient future in climate resiliency and sustainability. By 2030, insurance will be reshaped by AI-driven automation, real-time risk assessment, and sustainable business models. Insurers must embrace innovation and collaborate with partners like Wipro to enhance efficiency, improve customer experiences, and navigate emerging climate and technology risks. With a deep understanding of emerging technologies and their potential to disrupt industries, Varun drives innovation and digital transformation for Wipro clients . His expertise in crafting and executing technology strategies, combined with his focus on emerging tech and co-innovation, helps organizations achieve sustainable growth and competitive advantage.

title: eBay Sneaker Fees Explained. A Seller’s Complete Breakdown
summary: Learn how eBay sneaker fees work, what you’ll pay to sell sneakers in 2026, and how to reduce those fees and profit more.
body_text: While eBay sneaker selling fees vary greatly based on factors such as selling price and store subscription level, you are generally looking at a 7% to 13.6% fee . This is a pretty wide range, so let’s break down exactly what fees to expect as an eBay sneaker seller, how to calculate your fees , how other platforms compare, and strategies to help you keep more of your earnings. Main Takeaways eBay charges lower fees for sneaker sales of $150 or more. Final value fees range from 7% to 13.6%, depending on sale price and whether you have a store subscription. Authenticity Guarantee applies to eligible sneaker sales over $100, which boosts buyer confidence, protects sellers, and saves sellers on final value fees. Compared to other platforms like StockX, GOAT, and Poshmark, eBay offers the best selling fees (especially on items over $150) Using strategies like smart pricing, cross listing , and eBay store subscriptions can help lower eBay shoe fees and maximize profits. What are eBay’s Sneaker Fees? Sneakers are one of the best selling items on eBay , but it’s important to clearly understand the fees involved to ensure you’re making a good profit. eBay’s sneaker fees fall into two categories: insertion and final value. Let’s break them down. Insertion Fees eBay’s insertion fee is what sellers pay to list an item on their platform, whether the item sells or not . It might be easier to think of it as a listing fee. While the fee is usually $0.35 per listing, eBay does give sellers 250 free listings per month. As a bonus, sneakers with a starting or Buy It Now price of $150 or more have waived insertion fees , which don't count towards your 250 free listings. But one thing to keep in mind is that fees apply per category. So if you decide to list in two categories, you will pay the insertion fee twice. Final Value Fees When it comes to eBay sneaker selling fees, the final value fee is the one you’ll want to pay the most attention to. That’s because final value fees are the biggest chunk of your eBay fees . The good news? If you’re selling higher value sneakers ($150+), the fees are lower. The bad news is the fees can be a little tricky to calculate. eBay calculates the final value fee based on the total amount of the sale , which includes: Item price Shipping charges collected from the buyer Handling charges Sales tax (if applicable) The two main factors that impact how much you pay are the sale price of the sneakers and whether you have a store subscription. In addition, there is a per-order fee on top of the final value fee: $0.30 for orders $10 or less, and $0.40 for orders over $10 . However, if you're selling sneakers priced $150 or more in the Men’s or Women’s Athletic Shoes categories, this per-order fee is waived. 📝 Note on Authenticity Guarantee Sales: Suppose your sneakers qualify for eBay’s Authenticity Guarantee, and you use the free shipping label provided. In that case, eBay does not charge a final value fee on the shipping cost, just on the item price and other applicable fees. More details on this are in the next section. Here’s a quick breakdown of current fees based on sale price and store level: Sale Price Seller Type Insertion Fee Per Order Fee Final Value Fee $150+ No store/starter Free (if listed in Men's/Women's > Athletic Shoes) $0 8% Basic, Premium, or Higher Free (if listed in Men’s/Women’s > Athletic Shoes) $0 7% <$150 No store/starter 0.35 after 250 free listings .40 13.6% Basic, Premium or Higher $0.35 per listing after free listings (depends on store type) .40 12.7% Other Fees to Watch The most common eBay shoe fees are detailed above, but one more fee may apply: the International Selling Fee. International Fee (1.65%) If you sell to a buyer outside the U.S., you may be charged an international fee of 1.65% of the total sale amount. This fee applies when: The buyer’s registered address is outside the U.S. or The item is being shipped internationally, and you're not using eBay International Shipping The good news is that if you use eBay International shipping , this fee is waived. This program simplifies shipping internationally by letting you ship your item to a U.S. based hub, and then eBay shipping takes care of customs, international delivery, and even return handling. eBay’s Authenticity Guarantee: How It Impacts Fees Image Source: eBay The Authenticity Guarantee is a free service for eligible sneakers priced at $100 or more . When an item qualifies, it’s sent to a professional authenticator before being shipped to the buyer. This protects both the buyer and seller and helps prevent counterfeit issues. The main benefits of this program include a boost in buyer confidence that they are buying authentic sneakers, extra protection for returns and claims, and the ability to stand out in search results with the Authenticity Guarantee badge. In addition, with this program buyers pay a flat $14.95 shipping fee (U.S. orders), but you don’t pay anything extra . In fact, the final value fee for the shipping cost is waived for Authenticity Guarantee orders, which ends up saving you money. How Does It Work? If your sneakers are eligible, eBay will automatically add them to the Authenticity Guarantee program. You’ll know your listing qualifies if it has the blue Authenticity Guarantee checkmark in the search results and listing page. Here’s how it works: You make a sale of an eligible pair of sneakers. eBay provides a prepaid FedEx shipping label, which you use to send the item to their authentication center. Once the item is received, it’s typically inspected within 2 days. During this inspection the authenticator: Verifies that the sneaker matches the listing title, description, and photos Performs a physical authentication check to confirm the item is genuine After inspection, one of two things happens: If the sneakers pass, they are shipped to the buyer via 2 day delivery If the sneakers don’t match the listing or can’t be authenticated , they are shipped back to you and the buyer is refunded This entire process is 100% free for sellers and is handled by eBay and its authentication partners. Eligibility and Requirements To qualify for the Authenticity Guarantee program, all of the following must apply: Sneakers are priced at $100+ (Note: eBay has expanded this to include select, highly coveted sneaker models starting at $75 ). High-Value Protection: If your sneakers sell for $750 or more , eBay automatically upgrades the final delivery to require a signature from the buyer to protect you against "item not received" claims. Buyers pay a flat $14.95 shipping fee , and eBay provides you with a prepaid FedEx shipping label to ship the shoes to the hub completely free of charge. Listing is in the Men’s, Women’s, or Kids' Athletic Shoes categories It cannot be marked as customized Sold by a US based seller to a buyer with a US, Canadian, or Australian address It cannot be marked as in-store pickup, local pickup, or having a military address. Sneakers must be on the list of eligible brands, including Nike, Adidas, Yeezy, Hoka, and more. Full list here . Seller Protections and Benefits One of the biggest benefits of the Authenticity Guarantee program is the added protection it gives sellers. Once your item is authenticated and shipped, you’re no longer responsible for authenticity-related issues. You’re also protected from fraudulent returns. If a buyer wants to return their sneakers, the item must first undergo re-authentication to ensure it’s still in the same condition. On top of that, listings with the Authenticity Guarantee badge tend to sell faster and for higher prices because buyers feel more confident buying from sellers backed by eBay’s program. How eBay’s Sneaker Fees Compare to Competitors If you want to sell sneakers online, eBay is the most cost-effective marketplace. In an effort to support and encourage high-end sneaker sellers, eBay’s sneaker fees are lowered for higher-priced sales ($150 or more), making it easily the most competitive marketplace in terms of low fees. Let’s compare the fees across a few resale platforms for a $200 pair of sneakers. Platform Seller Fee Fee for $200 sale Notes eBay 8% (no store or starter store) / 7% (basic store and up) $16/$14 Final value fee waived on shipping if eligible for Authenticity Guarantee StockX 7% - 9% based on your level $14 - $18 9% for Level 1 (under 12 sales or $5,000); 7% for Level 5 (800+ sales or $100k+). GOAT 9.5% + $5 $24 Commission increases if the seller rating is under 90. 2.9% cashout fee applies. Poshmark 20% $40 Why eBay is Best for Sneaker Sellers: Lowest fees for sneakers pried $150+ Authenticity Guarantee at no additional cost (for eligible items) Faster sales velocity thanks to a large buyer base Practical Example: Calculating Fees on eBay for a Sneaker Sale Confused about how to calculate eBay sneaker selling fees? Let’s break down exactly how much you’d pay on a $150 sale. We’ll be using this quick fee estimate formula: Net = Sale Price – (Sale Price × Final Value Fee %) Non-store seller Item Sale Price: $150 Final Value Fee: 8% of $150 = $12 Per Order Fee: Waived Insertion fee: Waived Total Fees: $12 Net Profit: $150 - $12 = $138 Basic Store Seller (& Higher) Item Sale Price: $150 Final Value Fee: 7% of $150 = $10.50 Per Order Fee: Waived Insertion fee: Waived Total Fees: $10.50 Net Profit: $150 - $12 = $139.50 If you want to double-check your numbers or factor in shipping costs, you can use a free tool like Vendoo’s eBay Fee Calculator . Strategies to Minimize Fees and Maximize Profits Selling eBay Shoes Want to keep more profit in your pockets? Here are some ways to reduce eBay sneaker fees and, as a result, make your sales more profitable. Price Strategically Remember that a sale at $150 triggers lower fees and waives the per order charge. So if you’re close to the $150 threshold, try bumping your price up and improving your listing to get that higher price. Use eBay Store Subscriptions A Basic Store subscription or higher reduces your final value fee and gives you more free listings each month. For sneakers under $150, you’ll reduce your final value fee from 13.6% to 12.7%, and for sneakers that sell over $150, you’ll reduce your final value fee from 8% to 7%. Leverage Free Insertions All sellers get 250 free listings per month, and sneakers priced at $100 or more don’t count against that limit. Staying within that range can help you avoid extra listing fees. Authenticity Guarantee Listings that qualify for Authenticity Guarantee show an official badge that can boost buyer trust, help your items sell faster, and potentially help them sell for a higher price. It also removes the final value fee on shipping when you use eBay's provided label. Offer Competitive Shipping Avoid overcharging for shipping. When buyers are already spending a lot of money on a pair of sneakers, an inflated shipping price can cause hesitation. By charging a flat fee of $14.95 or similar, your buyer won’t feel like they’re overpaying for shipping. Crosslist with Tools Selling across multiple marketplaces is one of the best ways to maximize your profit. Use a tool like Vendoo to help you list on additional marketplaces to help your items sell faster by getting them in front of a larger audience. Monitor Fee Updates eBay occasionally updates its fee structure. Make sure to bookmark the Seller Center and check any emails eBay sends to make sure you’re up to date and can adjust your strategy if any fee changes are made. The Bottom Line on eBay Sneaker Fees Selling sneakers can be a profitable side hustle, or eventful time business, especially when you truly understand eBay’s sneaker fees and use them to your advantage. By pricing strategically, using programs like Authenticity Guarantee , and focusing on sourcing and selling higher value items, you can reduce fees and keep more of your earnings. Compared to other platforms, eBay offers the lowest fees and fastest sales velocity, especially when you cross that $150 sweet spot. Now that you know how fees work, and how to minimize them, you can get to listing and keep more from every sale! For sneakers priced at $150 or more, eBay takes 8% for non-store sellers and 7% for Basic Store and above. Sneakers priced under $150 have higher fees: 13.6% for non-store sellers and 12.7% for Basic Store and above. Are eBay sneaker fees higher than other platforms? No, eBay sneaker selling fees are generally lower. This is especially true for sneakers that sell for over $150. Do I pay fees if my sneakers don’t sell? In most cases, no. Final Value Fees are only charged on items that sell. For insertion fees, eBay gives you 250 free listings per month, and sneakers priced at $100 or more don’t count towards that total. However, if you go over these limits, you may pay a $0.35 insertion fee. Is an eBay Store worth it for sneaker sellers? If you’re selling consistently, yes. A Basic store subscription costs $21.95/month and includes 1,000 free fixed priced listings. It also offers lower final value fees. These savings can really add up and more than cover the monthly fee if you sell enough. What sneakers are most profitable to sell on eBay? While many sneaker categories perform well, success depends on sourcing in-demand models and trends. Reviewing the top selling items on eBay can give you insight into which sneakers and styles are generating consistent sales.
